spans.title: The Old Campaigner
spans.blurb: A village spinster's window commands every secret in town, including the Major's unexplained wound, his Indian habits, and the lock of hair he thinks nobody sees him kiss.
spans.brokenNote: Otherwise a complete comic portrait, but the final sentence cuts off mid clause.

spans.title: Popping In on Diva
spans.blurb: Armed with two telltale chintz roses and a rumor about coal fines, a smiling caller sets out to make her dearest rival thoroughly uncomfortable.

books.pairNote: Different subjects entirely: one sketches the Major from a window, the other follows a needling social call on Diva.

spans.title: Five Feet of Water
spans.blurb: Through a cabin door left ajar, two girls overhear the captain confess what the crew already knows: the ship is leaking faster than the pumps can fight.

spans.title: Fifteen Miles After Dark
spans.blurb: A wrong carriage strands a girl fifteen miles from home with ninepence, a moonlit road, and rather too much confidence.

books.pairNote: Two unrelated tales drawn from an anthology of fifty two stories.

spans.title: Joey the Pedigree Pom
spans.blurb: A landlady's daughter parades seven little dogs upstairs for a lodger, saving for last a scrawny white Pom whose pedigree rests entirely on love.

spans.title: The Hat He Sat On
spans.blurb: He ruins her cheap hat on purpose, buys her a beautiful one, and then asks a question she believes she has no right to answer.
spans.spoilerNote: Reveals that the novelist Tanqueray courts and proposes marriage to the servant Rose, a turn the novel stages as a surprise to his circle.

books.pairNote: Two separate stages of the same courtship; the later scene deepens the earlier without repeating it.

spans.title: Gringalet Pleads His Case
spans.blurb: A greyhound raised from a bottle by his master's devoted servant invites himself along on an expedition, pleading with ears, paw, and beseeching eyes.

spans.title: The Listener in the Leaves
spans.blurb: Troubled by a forced suitor and a harsh stepfather, a girl climbs to her childhood refuge to think, and the wrong men stop beneath her branch.

spans.title: Standoff at the Door
spans.blurb: Dressed to walk out forever, she finds the doorway blocked by a smiling man certain that no little empress can defy him.
spans.brokenNote: Stops mid sentence at the climactic grapple, leaving the final action hanging.

books.pairNote: Separate episodes, though the longer one shows the lover the girl trusts in the shorter turned captor.

spans.title: Psalms and Scythes
spans.blurb: Fifty men come down a mountain at night, singing a psalm, carrying scythes and hatchets, to demand prisoners a militia will not release.

spans.title: A Message from Brande
spans.blurb: He knows who sent the telegram before he opens it. What he cannot explain is what becomes of it afterward.
spans.spoilerNote: Reveals the reach of Brande's telepathic power, which the novel discloses step by step.

spans.title: A Drop of Water
spans.blurb: On a dark sea, a host promises his guests a scientific amusement: he will unmake a single drop of water and let them watch.
spans.spoilerNote: Shows the annihilating power of Brande's science, which the novel builds toward gradually.

books.pairNote: Two distinct demonstrations of Brande's powers with no shared text or shared payoff.

spans.title: Into the Beggar King's Swamp
spans.blurb: A detective in hobo disguise is warned that men who fail inspection never leave the swamp. Then the blindfold goes on.
spans.spoilerNote: Plants the strong suspicion that the outlaw chief Hobo Harry is a woman, the identity mystery at the heart of the novel.

spans.title: Ridden Down
spans.blurb: A horseman answers an insult by riding a man into the dust before a shocked girl. The beaten man's apology hides a plan.

spans.title: Twelve Children on a Warship
spans.blurb: On an old anchored warship, a grizzled father raises twelve children, one of whom insists, quite calmly, that he can swim to shore.
